name: Ge'ez
note: Abugida: 33 consonants, each written in seven vowel orders, giving 231 syllables. Rows are consonants, columns are vowels; the shape of the base changes slightly in each order rather than taking a separate vowel sign.

letters.name: hä
letters.notes: Listed in first order, carrying the vowel ä. Each consonant has seven orders, one per vowel, written as changes to the same base shape.

letters.name: ḥä
letters.notes: Pronounced the same as ሀ in modern Amharic. It survives in historical spellings, so few cells begin words.

letters.name: śä
letters.notes: Pronounced the same as ሰ. Kept for etymological spelling, so most cells do not begin words.

letters.name: vä
letters.notes: Only in words taken from other languages, which is why most of the row has no everyday example.

letters.name: ḫä
letters.notes: Pronounced the same as ሀ. Historical spelling only.

letters.name: ñä
letters.notes: A genuine Amharic sound, but one that rarely begins a word.

letters.name: ḵä
letters.notes: Mostly an allophone of ከ; rare word-initially.

letters.name: ʿä
letters.notes: Pronounced the same as አ. Historical spelling only.

letters.name: ṗä
letters.notes: Almost entirely in words borrowed through Greek, such as ጳውሎስ.

letters.name: ḍä
letters.notes: Pronounced the same as ጸ. Historical spelling only.

letters.name: qʷä
letters.notes: A velar said with rounded lips. These take five of the seven orders, since a rounded u or o would be no different from plain u or o, which is why they sit outside the 231-cell syllabary. Modern Amharic writes most of them with the plain letter instead, so few cells have a common word.

letters.name: qʷə
letters.notes: A historical spelling; modern Amharic writes ቁጥር.

letters.name: qhʷä
letters.notes: Tigrinya; Amharic does not use this series.

letters.name: lʷä
letters.notes: A consonant said with rounded lips. Unlike the labiovelars these have one form only, not a series of five.
